title: Alignment workshop + All-Hands runbook and OKR flashcards (v0.1)
content:
Purpose / TL;DR:
- Prepare a compact, practiceable run for the upcoming alignment workshop (company all-hands + team breakout) focused on OKR handoff, risk signal sharing, and execution pledges.
- This doc is a lightweight rehearsal script + executive talking points + one-page OKR flashcards for stage presenters. Notified execs should review their flashcards by Mar 15.

High-level goals for the session:
1) Reconcile top-level company OKRs with team commitments (2–3 minute flashcards).
2) Surface binary go/no-go risk signals for Q2 launches (SLO, capacity, compliance).
3) Get rapid commitments (owner + date) for remediation work where risk != green.
4) Create the one-week post-allhands cadence (A: owners, B: evidence, C: follow-ups).

Audience and framing:
- Audience: entire company (engineering, product, ops, sales, CS) — ~150 people.
- Tone: pragmatic, engineering-first, short on slides, long on clear commitments.
- Emphasis: what we will ship, what we will not ship, where we need help.

Run order (90 minutes total):
- 0:00–0:05 Welcome + context (CEO) — 3 slides max (north star + one ask)
- 0:05–0:18 Exec highlights and changes to company OKRs (5 execs, 2m each) -> use flashcards (see "OKR flashcards" below)
- 0:18–0:30 Risk spotlight (SRE + Security) — 4 min SRE / 4 min Security / 4 min product mitigations
- 0:30–0:60 Team breakouts (by product lane) — 30m (5m quick report-out template)
- 0:60–0:78 Report-outs (3 teams x 6m) — focused on: top commit, blocker, resources needed
- 0:78–0:85 Call-to-action and signups (people ops + growth)
- 0:85–0:90 Close + housekeeping (OPS runbook links, postmortem cadence)

Rehearsal checklist (deadline Mar 16):
- Slides reduced to 1–3 bullets each, speakers have 2 practice runs. Owner: Priya.
- Flashcards handed to execs for review. Owner: Avery.
- Breakout facilitators assigned and given prompts. Owner: Diego.
- Tech check (Zoom, streaming, captions) scheduled. Owner: Elena.
- Post-handoff doc templates created (report-out template in drive). Owner: Samir.

OKR Flashcards (one-paragraph: objective + 3x measurable key results + 1 line on why it matters):
- Company Objective A: Make inferencing predictable and economical for scale deployments.
  - KR1: Reduce median hosted API tail latency (p95) by 15% for the top-10 customer routes by end of Q2.
  - KR2: Increase average utilization of Redwood Dedicated pools by 18% via autoscaling config recommendations.
  - KR3: Launch two quantization profiles with validated accuracy loss < 3% on key benchmarks.
  - Why: Lower latency and cost reduces churn and opens enterprise adoption.

- Company Objective B: Enterprise-ready private deployments at scale.
  - KR1: Complete two Private VPC pilots with SOC2 endpoint monitoring and KMS/HSM integration.
  - KR2: Publish hardened on-prem deployment guide and increase install success rate to 85% in lab tests.
  - KR3: Add audit logging and retention controls to the Console for all Private customers.
  - Why: Removing infra and security frictions is the gating factor for larger enterprise contracts.

Speaker guidance (brevity-first):
- Each flashcard = 2 minutes live. No wandering. Start with the one-sentence outcome we want. End with a single tangible ask (owner + timeline).
- Script example: "Outcome: Reduce p95 for core routes by 15% (KR). Plan: runtime kernel selection + targeted batching recommendations. Ask: SRE + Serving runtime to validate on canary by Apr 10 (Owners: Samir, Diego)."

Risk signals (prepopulated, bring evidence to stage):
- Capacity: Dedicated pool utilization >90% on peak windows in prod (evidence: DR telemetries + pool logs).
- Regression: Model quality drift on two prompt suites >5% BLEU drop.
- Compliance: KMS/HSM integration tests failing for one enterprise pilot.
- Observability: Console retention expiry causing missing traces for recent incidents.
- For each risk, teams should declare: Green / Watch / Red, and a 1-line mitigation.

Breakout prompts (each facilitator receives this):
- What is your single most important shipment in the next 6 weeks? Owner + date?
- What is the biggest blocker preventing that shipment? Who is needed?
- What would success look like (metrics)?
- If you had one ask of the company (people/time/budget), what is it?

Report-out template (5 minutes):
- One-line priority (shipment + date)
- One blocker (who/what)
- Clear ask (person or team + timeframe)

Post-event follow-ups (72-hour loop):
- Consolidated report-out doc published to Confluence and linked into the OKR tracker. (Owner: Product Ops)
- Any Red risks escalate to Exec triage; set 72-hour action plan. (Owner: SRE lead)
- Assign owners in the OKR tracker for any new KRs created from breakouts. (Owner: OKR program manager)

Execution pledges (example entries to collect during the event):
- "Serve runtime will complete kernel tuning for MPT-like shapes by Apr 7." — Owner: Diego Ramirez — Evidence: bench runs and canary plan.
- "Customer Success will onboard two more Dedicated pilots by May 1." — Owner: Priya Patel — Evidence: signed SOWs.

Quick emcee script highlights:
- Opening: "We’ll keep this tight; the goal is clarity not applause. If you leave with three names and dates, we did our job."
- Transition to breakouts: "Breakouts: answer the 4 prompts. Facilitators will keep you strict on time."
- Close: "Within 72 hours we’ll publish the consolidated report and schedule a 30-minute triage for any red risks."

Logistics and helpful links (prepopulate):
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OPS/Bridge+Week+Playbook
- OKR tracker: https://docs.redwood.company/okr-tracker (editable)
- Rehearsal Zoom: Tue Mar 16 10:00–11:00 PT — link shared in #allhands channel
- Tech contact: Elena Morozova (elena@redwood.company)

Open questions / decision needed by Mar 14:
- Do we fold the dedicated product roadmap into Company Objective A or keep as separate KR set? (Recommendation: fold; reduces cross-silo asks.)
- Are we comfortable publishing the quantization profiles as experimental (yes/no)? (Ops concern: change protocol for hosted models).
- Who will own the final master slide deck? (Nomination: Priya + Avery co-owners)

Notes to self (working/rough):
- Keep slide deck under 12 slides. Prefer speaker notes over bullets.
- Avoid deep technical demos in the main stage — move to post-event office hours.
- Add a one-page quickreference for execs with "Top 3 questions we expect" and canned answers.

Action item summary (owners + due dates):
- Speaker flashcards reviewed by speakers: Avery (due Mar 15)
- Rehearsal session scheduled: Elena (Mar 16)
- Breakout facilitator list finalized: Diego (Mar 14)
- Consolidated report template created: Samir (Mar 18)

End of runbook — keep this doc for iterative rehearsal notes. Rename to v0.2 when slides locked."
